scope: Add an explicit, bounded route-check action for an aggregator listing. Follow only public HTTPS redirects to a verified employer domain or a recognized ATS destination whose tenant matches persisted company evidence. Display a redacted candidate without changing the user's route selection or submitting an application.

environment.frontend: local Vite production build and connected Chromium
environment.delivery: local-only; no push or hosted automation

checks.evidence: 43 tests passed, including verified employer/ATS targets, exact tenant matching, query redaction, unrelated-host rejection, robots denial, unresolved redirects, API integration with a synthetic redirect transport, selected-route preservation, and regressions in the shared public client.
92 frontend test files and 533 tests passed.
TypeScript check and Vite production build passed. Existing advisory: generated JavaScript chunk is 738.60 kB.

Connected local Chromium exercised the explicit route-check button, rendered the returned verified ATS destination, kept preparation enabled, and submitted preparation with the unchanged user-selected aggregator route. The check response was intercepted locally; no external network request or application submission occurred.

checks.evidence: Changed Python modules compiled and the candidate diff had no whitespace errors.

not_run: Live requests to employer or ATS sites; all redirect responses were synthetic and network-intercepted.
Hosted Actions, hosted review, or external certification (disabled by local-only policy).
limitations: Resolution is an explicit user action from the job preparation view and is bounded to an 8-second client deadline and the existing three-redirect cap. It is not persisted, does not create/select a new route, and the destination remains a candidate for user review.
Only verified employer domains and a bounded set of recognized ATS hosts with a matching verified tenant are eligible redirect destinations; intermediary hosts without that evidence fail closed.
Automatic external submission remains disabled, so an automatic pre-submission gate cannot be exercised. MJ-REQ-267 remains PARTIAL.
PostgreSQL, full Python suite, hosted checks, and live remote-site behavior remain unverified.
safety: Route checking occurs only after the user clicks the button; job reads and page loads perform no redirect check.

The existing public client enforces HTTPS, globally routable DNS results, pinned vetted addresses, bounded response/header sizes, cancellation, and deadlines. The route probe also checks robots.txt for each followed origin and rejects unverified cross-origin destinations.
The request sends no cookies or credentials. Remote page content is not saved; query strings and fragments are omitted from returned candidate links.
No route is automatically substituted or persisted. Application preparation keeps the route explicitly selected by the user and does not submit externally.
